newsitem.title: JAPAN: Citizen seeks higher sales from core watch business.
newsitem.headline: Citizen seeks higher sales from core watch business.

text.p: Japan's Citizen Watch Co Ltd said on Monday that it aims to boost revenues in its mainstream wristwatch business as it feels the world watch market still has room to expand.

Hiroshi Haruta, president of the leading watch manufacturer, told reporters the company needs to reconsider its strategy of boosting profits from non-watch sectors to the same level as that of its watch business.
"We need to change our previous belief that the watch market is already a mature one and that it is difficult to increase revenues from the sector," Haruta said.
"It is important to expand revenues from our watch sector, where investments will have a quick impact," he said.

Haruta added that in addition to raising overall revenues by boosting sales in the wristwatch sector, Citizen would in the long term need to focus on its non-watch sectors so as to make sure the company has a stable business base.

Demand for inexpensive wristwatches will grow in areas such as Asia, the Middle East and Russia, while demand for more expensive, value-added watches will grow in developed nations as well as in Asia's emerging economies, he said.
In the year to March 31, 1997, 53.8 percent of Citizen's net sales came from its watch and watch parts sectors, with the rest from information equipment, such as floppy disc drives.
Cost-cutting in the watch sector and the weak yen helped push up group net profit by about 30 percent to 9.76 billion yen ($86.3 million) in 1996/97, offsetting damage from falling computer sales.
Citizen also said it would not curb its transactions with its main bank, Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd (DKB), which has been embroiled in a payoff and racketeer scandal.
"As the bank now faces tough challenges (due to the scandal) we can expect that it will turn out to be a good company after all," Haruta said.
Citizen chairman Michio Nakajima told the same briefing that Citizen has avoided having any dealings with racketeers.
"It is important to make a decision at the beginning to avoid any links with racketeers. Once you have any form of relations with them, it becomes hard to cut the ties," he said. ($1=113 yen)
